answer: One concrete mechanism: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because velvet only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, vine is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any falcon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
